key_insight: The paper shows that IQP quantum kernels have an RKHS expressivity controlled by a finite set of circuit-defined frequencies and the bandwidth hyperparameter, leading to distinct localized, multimodal, and periodic function regimes.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical rule for tuning quantum kernel bandwidth to match known data structure, improving when and how quantum feature maps are likely to help in real machine learning tasks.
method: Derived a Fourier-based characterization of the RKHS generators for IQP feature maps.
Identified accessible frequencies from the circuit structure and showed how bandwidth scales them.
Validated the theory on synthetic classification and anomaly-detection benchmarks, compared with a Gaussian kernel.
evidence_signal: Experiments on synthetic datasets with controlled periodic and multimodal structure reproduced the three predicted expressivity regimes across data dimensions and feature-map configurations in both supervised and unsupervised settings.
watch_item: The benefit depends on a strong match between the kernel’s accessible frequencies and the true data structure, so poorly chosen bandwidth or mismatched data patterns may reduce or eliminate gains over classical kernels.
paper_title: Expressivity of IQP Feature-Map Quantum Kernels via Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
